name: Representative democracy
summary: Representative democracy is government in which citizens choose officials by election to make laws and run the state for them, rather than deciding directly. Its defenders, from Madison to Mill, hold that delegation filters opinion, guards against majority faction and lets large societies govern themselves while remaining answerable to voters. It prescribes a form of rule, not an economic or cultural programme.
scope: The liberal-constitutional mainstream, based on Madison's Federalist No. 10 and Mill's Considerations on Representative Government, as summarised in the Wikipedia and Stanford entries. Excludes direct, participatory, soviet and corporatist alternatives. Most social and economic statements are left to party competition, so many answers are neutral or low-confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Health policy is left to whoever wins elections; the system itself favours no side.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are an ordinary policy dispute for elected legislatures, not a commitment of the system.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Representative government is compatible with both market-liberal and social-democratic majorities.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalisation is something electorates may choose or reject; the form of government takes no side.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax rates are set by elected majorities, and adherents range across the economic spectrum.

unions-good.rationale: The form of government says nothing on unions; adherents split by party.

property-fundamental.rationale: Madison treats unequal property as the source of faction and wants it protected, but adherents differ on how hard it should be to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation level is a matter for electoral competition, not for the system's definition.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare size is contested between parties inside representative systems.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is an economic choice outside what the system prescribes.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: limits on government power and accountability to voters make adherents wary of surveillance, though security trade-offs split them.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is decided by legislatures and is not settled by the form of government.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: SEP treats speech as a right democracy protects, but adherents disagree on hate-speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Mill has the legislature watch and control the executive, and Madison fears concentrated power; bypassing gridlock cuts against that.

state-harmful.rationale: Representative democracy exists to make state power answerable through elections, so calling the state unnecessary is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is a policy dispute within representative systems.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security funding is decided by elected governments; the system is silent.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Moral-policy questions are left to legislatures; no stated position.

decide-locally.rationale: Madison favours dividing matters between national and local legislatures, but adherents differ on how local.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is outside the definition of the system.

traditional-family.rationale: Family values are left to voters and parties.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: A social-policy matter decided by legislatures, with adherents split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Contested by parties within representative democracies; no position follows from the system.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents range from secular to religious; the system is neutral.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Remedial policy is contested between parties.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A theoretical claim the system does not address.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Culture policy is left to electoral politics.

gradual-change.rationale: Madison and Mill favour change through deliberating assemblies and respect for institutions, though Mill also wants reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels are a standing party dispute within representative democracies.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents split between sovereignty-minded and internationalist positions.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is decided by elected governments; no stated position.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign-policy stance is not defined by the system.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents are split; the system says nothing on it.

open-borders.rationale: Not an issue the system addresses; most adherents accept border control as policy.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental trade-offs are left to electoral choice.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate response is an ordinary policy fight between parties in representative systems, so adherents split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources say nothing about technology; adherents hold views from techno-optimist to sceptical.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy mix is chosen by elected governments, and the sources take no side on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Change is meant to come through elections and assemblies, though Mill's emphasis on consent leaves room for resisting tyranny.

experts-over-public.rationale: SEP notes Mill's plural voting for the expert, but mainstream representative democracy keeps elected officials accountable to the public, not experts.

central-planning.rationale: The form of government is silent on economic organisation.

socialized-markets.rationale: An economic question that electorates may decide either way.

land-value-tax.rationale: A fiscal proposal, not a feature of the system.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance tax levels are set by legislatures and divide adherents along party lines.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare design is for legislatures to settle.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is decided by elected governments.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial strategy is left to electorates; adherents run from market liberals to interventionists.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Madison accepts unequal property as a given, so wide distribution is not a stated aim.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from Madison's treatment of property as the basis of liberty and faction; abolition would be seen as unrealistic.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary arrangements are outside the system's definition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: representation through parties and legislatures is the norm, not state-organised class bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Competitive elections among parties are the defining feature, so single-party rule is the opposite.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Parliamentary monarchies count as representative democracies and republics do too, so adherents are genuinely split.

democracy-best.rationale: Mill calls representative government the ideally best form of polity, and adherents answer bad voter choices with institutional checks and regular elections rather than by rejecting democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Madison holds pure democracies are turbulent and prefers delegation to representatives, and Mill says an assembly should control rather than govern directly.

workers-councils.rationale: Power rests on elected legislatures chosen by all citizens, not on class-based councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Madison values a large union but adherents differ on secession rights.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rulers are chosen by voters, not born to rule; Mill's expertise claims are about plural votes and commissions, not natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Peaceful transfer is the norm but adherents differ over absolute pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: not a theme of the sources, and civic deliberation is prized over war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship and neutral public procedures, though some systems keep established churches.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Legislators answer to voters, not scripture; some religious democrats differ.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: state institutions accountable to elected bodies are assumed.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is not defined by the system.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: citizenship and equal political rights are the basis of representation, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Madison sees factions as manageable inside representative institutions, not as driving history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distributive goals are decided at the ballot box.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land rights are a matter for legislation and courts, and the sources give no stance.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are a contested policy question; the system itself implies nothing.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: representation is organised by electorates and states, not civilisations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Madison accepts self-interest as human nature but does not call it morally good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Madison's protection of individual rights against majorities points the other way.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lie outside the political form, and adherents hold varied views.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not discussed in the sources and adherents are split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: the system is a product of modern societies and its defenders do not reject them.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pace of technological change is not a concern of the system; adherents differ.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics is left to legislatures, and the sources are silent.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Accountability runs through elected humans, so replacing their decisions with algorithms conflicts with it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources do not address encryption; adherents balance liberty and security differently.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mill treats progress as a criterion of good government.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mill judges governments by their effects on citizens, but pragmatism versus principle splits adherents.

direct-action.rationale: The ideology holds that change should go through elections and legislatures.

means-match-ends.rationale: Mill wants citizens trained for self-government through participation, but the sources do not frame it as a means-ends principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not part of any representative-democratic program and incompatible with its institutions at scale.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: SEP presents representation itself as a division of labour, so adherents accept it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: How goods are distributed is settled by voters and legislators, not by the form of government.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic organisation is left to electoral choice, so the system has no stance on profit versus use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred from Madison accepting property differences as a given rather than exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by a class over others contradicts equal voting rights and minority protections.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is outside the political form and not addressed by the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Theories of imperialism are not part of the ideology; adherents hold varied views.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxes are levied by elected legislatures, which is the system's legitimating claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill supports it elsewhere, but representative democracy as such does not.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Madison discusses rights of individuals and of minorities, so adherents are split.

conscription.rationale: Military service is decided by elected governments; liberal democracies differ on it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The system rests on voice through elections as the check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are treated as members who vote, not customers who leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mill stresses developing citizens' capacities, but the sources do not settle material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Elected officials hold formal authority; claims of hidden power are populist critiques.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from equal political standing of all citizens.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation of individuals through elected parties or candidates is the standard model; corporatist bodies are an alternative.

total-state.rationale: Limits on government and a protected private sphere are central.

national-rebirth.rationale: Palingenetic nationalism is not a theme of representative democracy, whose focus is procedure.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The sources do not discuss expansion; Mill-style consent of the governed cuts against forced annexation, but adherents vary.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on election and law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Legal serfdom contradicts the equal citizenship that elected representation presupposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: SEP's epistemic defences of democracy assume that some answers are better than others.

universal-morality.rationale: Adherents divide between rationalist and pluralist views.

single-common-good.rationale: Madison and Mill build institutions to balance competing interests and factions rather than find one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A national-homeland claim is outside the political form, and adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship rules for diasporas are a policy dispute, not defined by the system.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is left to legislatures and is not covered by the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is outside the political system.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding is a party dispute within representative democracies.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal stance is chosen by elected governments, and adherents differ.

economic-freedom.rationale: Madison links liberty and property, but adherents differ on this claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Madison wants institutions that work even without virtuous rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mill defends self-government as the ideal, but the full national claim is not stated in the sources I read.

force-without-un.rationale: The sources do not discuss the UN; adherents differ on unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Epistemology is outside the political form, and religious and secular democrats both accept the system.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is a contested policy question.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements are disputed between parties, not decided by the form of government.

class-collaboration.rationale: Madison sees interests being balanced; the sources do not call for partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not a position found in sources; inferred as foreign to the tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western bloc politics are not part of this ideology.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organisation is not addressed; representation here is by electoral district or party.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from equal rights and universal suffrage.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred from Madison's acceptance of commercial interests.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legal racial classification contradicts the equal political standing of all citizens that SEP ties to democracy.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Madison and Mill see class factions as a danger to be checked, not the state's essence.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is left to elected governments.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integration policy divides adherents, and the sources do not speak to it.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim not supported by the system's defenders.

proportional-representation.rationale: Mill backed Hare's proportional scheme, but representative systems with single-member districts are equally standard.

national-mission.rationale: Exporting a form of government is not a stated feature of representative democracy; adherents differ.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Whether society structurally favours men is disputed among adherents, and the system takes no side.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Madison warns that elections can be won by intrigue, but defenders treat that as a risk to guard against.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from equal rights and bodily liberty.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from legal accountability of government.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Scope of government is a matter for elections.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging marriage across racial lines conflicts with equal citizenship and liberty.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: SEP presents democracy as treating persons as equals and Mill grounds it in citizens' interest.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no bearing on representative democracy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A historical-interpretation question that the sources do not address.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Whether civil law is uniform is a policy question debated in democracies with religious law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from freedoms of association and belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Animal-slaughter law is decided by legislatures, and the sources are silent.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious teaching in schools is handled differently across democracies, and adherents split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Leninist argument for a strong state, at odds with limited accountable government.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mill says ultimate sovereignty rests in the community and SEP traces legitimate authority to consent in Locke.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not part of the ideology; adherents differ.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority contradicts equal citizenship and rights against majorities that Madison wanted protected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The non-aggression principle is libertarian, not part of this ideology, whose state uses coercion by law.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Madison welcomes competing interests, but not as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: SEP discusses internal limits protecting democratic process, but adherents split on banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Madison's fear of arbitrary majorities fits, but the term is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Madison's division of power and constitutional courts limiting legislatures support checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Elected representatives of citizens replace a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priority is decided at the ballot box, and the system itself is neutral.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A housing policy that parties fight over in elections.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is a party dispute, and the sources say nothing on it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A Malthusian claim outside the political form; adherents differ.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Madison argues that a variety of interests protects liberty.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Election is the defining method; sortition is the contrasting Athenian one.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from limits on majorities and rights.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are an economic policy question open to electoral choice.

party-controls-media.rationale: Free speech is a condition of the democratic process.

party-commands-army.rationale: The military answers to the elected government, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship waiting periods vary across democracies and are party issues.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: sources do not cover pay; adherents generally want capable candidates.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Burke's trustee model argues against binding, parties often do enforce discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Madison favours a larger union, but adherents split over supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Mill has the legislature control the executive, but presidential systems differ.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance falls outside the state form of representative democracy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority is held by elected representatives.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism belongs to Leninism and is not a representative-democratic stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: SEP counts free expression as a condition of the democratic process, so moral censorship of art is disfavoured.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from Madison's fear of entrenched power.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is listed as a direct measure, but adherents split on it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is chosen by elected governments, with no position in the system.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from Madison's protection of property as a basis of liberty; banning rental would be seen as excessive.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militia versus standing army is a historical debate, but nothing in the sources fixes the answer.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A cultural or agrarian claim unrelated to the form of government.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a foreign-policy question that the sources do not address.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A populist claim about graduates; the sources do not take it up.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is outside the political form, and adherents differ.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is decided by legislatures, with adherents on both sides.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a party dispute in democracies.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science curriculum disputes are fought politically, and the system takes no side.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law divides adherents and is outside the sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Jus sanguinis versus jus soli varies between democracies.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are a policy matter, with adherents on both sides.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions are argued case by case in democracies, so adherents split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill defends this in On Liberty, but representative democracy as such does not.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt policy is not addressed and divides adherents.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A dependency-theory claim outside this ideology.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from consent and elected assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mill judges government by developing citizens, and SEP counts political rights as conditions of democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are debated among adherents and not covered by the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defence doctrine is left to elected governments.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Directly elected presidents and parliament-chosen heads of state are both common.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Contested between technocratic and democratic views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise is a diplomatic question outside the political form.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Madison protects property as a right but adherents differ on whether it is justified only by the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist historical dispute not addressed by representative democracy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation standards are for legislatures to set; adherents differ.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance commitments are chosen by elected governments, and adherents differ.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from consent of the governed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations differ across democracies, so adherents split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Parliamentary systems often have symbolic heads of state, presidential systems do not.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources do not address secession; adherents differ over the use of force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements are constitutional design choices that the sources do not address.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rulers hold office by election and are answerable, so divine status has no place in the form.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is a party dispute within democracies.

character-from-environment.rationale: Mill stresses institutions shaping character, but this is not a general claim.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Madison's republic and Mill's controlled executive mean rulers are bound by constitutional law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not a political-form question, and the sources are silent.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Madison mixes powers but not social orders; adherents split.

leader-cult.rationale: Rulers are accountable officials, not embodiments of the nation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are legal-policy questions open to disagreement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine with no counterpart in representative democracy.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is decided by legislatures, and adherents differ widely.

refugee-return.rationale: Return rights are a diplomatic issue not covered by the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from Mill's view that governments rest on the consent of the governed, not on ethnic kinship claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Criminalising religious exit contradicts the freedoms of belief and association SEP links to democracy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Incompatible with equal citizenship and liberty.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is chosen by elected governments, with adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not part of the ideology.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy arrangements are constitutional choices that the sources do not address.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy is outside the political form.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis, not a representative-democratic claim.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is for legislatures, and the sources do not speak to it.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are fought over between parties in representative systems.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutions and courts can limit legislatures and Madison fears majority faction.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are a contested electoral-design question.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is a rare policy, not part of the form of government.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-treaty content is decided by elected governments, and adherents split.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Guevarist idea for socialist economies; unconnected to representative democracy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Insurrectionary foco theory contradicts the principle that power is won through elections.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Election replaces inheritance, but constitutional monarchies persist.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum emphasis is a policy dispute.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill argues self-government is the ideal, though he accepted tutelage for backward peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Civic education aims differ between parties and adherents.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a party-political dispute.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed and adherents differ.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: An economic-theory claim outside this ideology.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Foreign cultural policy is left to elected governments.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency strategies are outside the political form.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis with no place in representative democracy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is a party dispute between libertarian and egalitarian democrats.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional limits and Madison's concern for rights against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: An international-law question not addressed by the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Wikipedia defines it by elected representatives and Mill treats rule by the community through representatives as the ideal.

minority-veto.rationale: Madison's faction and Mill's majority rule with minority representation reject minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from limited constitutional government and Mill's rejection of despotism, so resisting a ruler who breaks the constitution is plausible.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mill says the assembly controls the government, but constitutional courts also limit it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is outside the political form, and adherents differ.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal-welfare law is left to legislatures.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: An aristocratic ethic not part of representative democracy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mill says active citizens develop moral and intellectual qualities.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim that representative democracy does not state.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis outside this ideology.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A world-systems claim that adherents mostly do not hold as a doctrine.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the equal citizenship that makes naturalised citizens eligible for election in most democracies.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question, irrelevant to the ideology.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not part of this ideology.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not part of the form of government.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from equal political rights of all citizens.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Whether constitutions enshrine anti-fascism varies across democracies, and adherents split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: defenders of competitive elections generally condemn all one-party dictatorships, though the sources do not say so.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute that representative democracy takes no position on.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are fought politically, with adherents on both sides.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Social-policy priorities are left to voters and parties.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Mill says forms depend on a people's readiness, but representative government is held as the ideal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The military under elected civilian control is the norm.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care-work policy is contested between parties and not a system commitment.

filial-duty.rationale: Family ethics are outside the political form.

office-by-exam.rationale: Mill favoured examinations for public service but the claim "rather than election" divides adherents.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Investment screening is a party dispute in democracies.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is decided by legislatures with adherents on both sides.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burke's trustee view and Madison's filtering of opinion reject binding mandate.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is a party dispute, not a feature of the form of government.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure is outside the sources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Mill's assembly controls the government and legislatures hold the purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is contested between parties.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership limits are left to legislatures.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination doctrine is disputed across democracies.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cultural criticism not part of the political form.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert-action policy is left to elected governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the consent of the governed, since an invasion to reverse a people's political choice violates it.

corporate-influence.rationale: SEP discusses elite capture via campaign funding, but adherents split on how serious.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: NGO funding rules are contested between parties.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family policy is decided by elected governments.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property limits are policy disputes.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is a party dispute and not a system commitment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: adherents often cite the argument, but the sources did not discuss it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: SEP says authority rests on consent in Locke.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources are silent; adherents differ over whether intervention is ever justified.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a labour-movement question.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Treating a minority as a conspiracy contradicts equal citizenship.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is decided by legislatures and is not addressed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the accountability of elected government to the voters who choose it.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not part of the ideology.

informal-organisation.rationale: Political action is channelled through parties and elections, not small informal groups, in the form described.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty versus international law is a live dispute among democrats.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship regardless of religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A tributary order foreign to democratic states.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not address the distinction; most democracies protect all private property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War stance is contested among adherents.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are party disputes.

religion-illusion.rationale: A Marxist claim; representative democracy allows both believers and unbelievers.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A historical judgement that adherents may or may not accept.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Feminist economics is contested between parties and outside the form.

socialized-care.rationale: Care provision is left to party competition.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not part of the ideology.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty questions are left to courts and legislatures.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Utopian communitarianism is not part of the ideology.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from equal rights of minority members to live where they are.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way claims are not part of the ideology, which is compatible with market or social economies.

historical-land-claim.rationale: A national-claim question outside the political form.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: democratic defenders accept the historical record, though speech-protection debates vary.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the liberty and equal rights that representative democracies mostly protect.

suppress-opposition.rationale: SEP names freedom of speech and association as conditions of democracy and loyal opposition is mentioned.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from freedom of belief and expression as conditions of democratic process.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mill says governing for one's own good is bad, but sources are unclear.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine unrelated to representative democracy.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Removal of rulers by force on religious grounds rejects the principle that rulers change through election.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Madison and Mill prefer representation to direct popular decision-making, though Mill values citizen participation in public functions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A theory of oppression not addressed by the ideology.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal recognition is decided by legislatures, with adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics are left to legislatures and voters.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Representative democracy is organised around competing parties, but whether left and right still matter is disputed.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept outside this ideology.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship and freedom of belief.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Representative government rests on election and consent of the governed, as Madison and Mill argue, not divine right.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The system prescribes a form of rule and leaves church-state questions to elected legislatures.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Contract and employment law are matters for legislatures to decide; the system itself favours no side.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic order is left to party competition and the system takes no side.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Defence policy is for elected governments; the system takes no side, though civilian control of the military is assumed.

rich-first.rationale: Development policy is an ordinary electoral dispute, not a commitment of the system.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alliance choices are decided by elected governments; the system itself is neutral.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Representative democracy rests on officials chosen by election, which hereditary succession of a state leader contradicts, though constitutional monarchies coexist with it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: An economic arrangement outside the form of rule the ideology prescribes.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic policy is left to elected governments, so the system itself takes no side.

property-franchise.rationale: Mill and Madison both discussed limits on franchise, but modern representative democracy rests on broad suffrage; Mill himself favoured widening it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: A social theory outside the form of rule the ideology prescribes.

reification.rationale: A Marxist claim about capitalism, which the ideology leaves to party competition.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The ideology values a free press but takes no side on the class critique of ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Liberal-constitutional representative government makes laws through the legislature and holds rulers to them under constitutional limits.

racial-franchise.rationale: Its premise that citizens choose representatives is incompatible with limiting the vote to one ethnic group, as Mill's case for broad representation shows.

online-participation.rationale: Delegation through elected officials is the core form; online deliberation could supplement or compete with it, and adherents differ.

open-government-data.rationale: Accountability of elected officials to voters favours open records, though the sources do not state this directly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The ideology prescribes only a form of rule, but its liberal-constitutional mainstream protects religious freedom; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: A private social practice outside the form of government; no position in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Madison's design relies on elected representatives to refine opinion rather than randomly chosen groups, so sortition rivals it, though assemblies could advise.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religion is outside the ideology's scope.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Madison treats unequal property as a source of faction but the system itself takes no stand on wealth limits; inferred from Federalist No. 10.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military personnel rules are left to elected legislatures; the sources do not address the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-constitutional commitment to freedom of conscience and speech as conditions of democracy; state-promoted unbelief conflicts with it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: representative government makes laws through elected bodies and relies on the state to enforce them, so it assumes policing and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Madison and Mill worry about majority faction and want minorities represented, but neither endorses mandatory executive power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Welfare delivery is a matter for party competition, not for the form of government.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are a contested design choice among defenders of representation; the sources discuss recall but not term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Representation rests on electing trustees who use their own judgment, which Madison says refines opinion; continuously revocable per-issue delegation cuts against that filter.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Risk priorities are left to elected governments; the sources do not address them.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal rules of religious bodies lie outside the system, which is neutral on them.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship in the liberal tradition; Mill argued for marital equality elsewhere, though not in the cited work.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The form of government says who sits in the legislature, not who votes; franchise rules vary among its defenders, so it is neutral.

rent-control.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not an economic programme, so it is neutral on rent policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not an economic programme, so it is neutral on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Constitutional representative government with free associations does not call for drilled national youth; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: A question of defence policy, not of the form of government; neutral.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: A question of defence policy, not of the form of government; neutral.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not an economic programme, so it is neutral.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Madison and Mill treat politics as managing competing interests through institutions, not a cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

god-not-male.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Madison in Federalist No. 10 designs representation to guard against faction and protect minorities from majority domination (s2).

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Outside its scope as a form of rule; neutral.

independent-unions.rationale: A form of government, not an economic programme; union independence is left to ordinary politics.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The system is neutral on economic systems; it prescribes how rulers are chosen, not what society is called.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public or private ownership is left to elected legislatures.

second-chamber.rationale: Madison and Mill favour institutional checks that refine opinion and guard against majority faction, which bicameral designs serve, but the form does not require a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership of production is a policy question for elected bodies, not a commitment of the system.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Leaving decisions to local assemblies with delegates who only coordinate is a direct-democratic model, which representative democracy sets itself against; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy is an ordinary policy dispute, not a commitment of the system.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory policy is left to elected governments.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding is left to elected governments.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Left to legislatures; the system itself favours no side.

online-anonymity.rationale: Left to legislatures; the system itself favours no side.

person-over-state.rationale: The liberal-constitutional tradition holds that government exists to serve citizens and protect individual rights; inferred from Mill and Madison.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The system takes no stand on human nature beyond citizens' capacity to choose rulers.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Representative systems exist as both federal and unitary, so the form does not decide it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Madison's Federalist No. 10 worries about factions pursuing partial interests against the common good, and representation is meant to refine them; inferred, applied to race by analogy.

racial-pride.rationale: Outside the scope of a form of government.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Foreign policy is left to elected governments.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Representative democracy prescribes a form of rule, not a theory of nationhood, so it is indifferent.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the principle of representing all citizens equally; Mill-style theory favours representing opinions, though some systems have used communal rolls.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule and takes no position on foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not economic or social programmes.

pollution-taxes.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not economic programmes.

future-generations.rationale: It is silent on intergenerational duties, though critics note elections favour the short term.

women-distinct-values.rationale: It is silent on the question; representation theory concerns how to represent citizens, not what values groups bring.

arms-reduction.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule and takes no position on armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from accountability of government to voters through the legislature, which Mill describes as watching and controlling the government.

capital-controls.rationale: It prescribes a form of rule, not economic programmes.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-constitutional view that the state holds legitimate force under law; the sources do not address armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: in the Madison and Mill tradition, elected governments decide on war, so individual soldiers' refusal sits poorly with civilian authority.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The form of government says nothing about wage-setting; left to party competition.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: An economic policy question left to party competition; no position follows from the form of rule.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Left to elected majorities; Madison and Mill do not address fiscal rules, though constitutional limits are consistent with the tradition.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A policy question left to elected governments; the form of rule is silent on it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Representative democracy works through constitutional elected institutions and changes them by lawful means, so smashing the state is incompatible.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The form of rule does not prescribe an economic system; the sources do not discuss it.

nature-as-capital.rationale: An economic and environmental policy question left to party competition.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: Madison and Mill treat the state as a civic, constitutional order, not a sacred community; the sources do not address it directly.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A fiscal policy question left to party competition.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A policy question the form of rule does not settle.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the liberal tradition of individual rights; Madison and Mill do not discuss human nature in these terms.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Mill's concern for an informed public and open debate; the sources do not discuss public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Representative democracy is a form of government and takes no view on religious truth; inferred from its purely procedural scope.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is left to party competition; the sources describe no position on it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Defence policy is decided by elected governments; nothing in the doctrine settles unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: Representative systems permit any party, including labour parties, but do not call for one; inferred from party competition being left open.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional protection of individual rights against custom and majorities that the liberal-constitutional tradition stresses.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the equal citizenship and equality of persons that Stanford's account treats as the basis of democracy.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A question of linguistics and identity that representative democracy does not address.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Whether courts or agencies handle pollution is left to elected legislatures; the doctrine takes no side.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Mill and Madison place lawmaking in elected assemblies answerable to voters, so an unelected chiefs' body fits poorly; inferred rather than stated.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The trade-off is left to elected majorities and constitutional limits; the doctrine prescribes no priority.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Fixed sentences are a policy choice for legislatures; adherents split between legislative control and judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Immigration and language rules are left to party competition.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Rule of government by elected representatives is silent on labour law; policy is left to party competition.

voter-id.rationale: Electoral administration is left to elected legislatures; adherents fall on both sides, as the form of rule says nothing on ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Madison's argument in Federalist 10 for protecting minority factions and Mill's liberal framework favour no state-preferred sect; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Representative democracy defines itself by officials chosen by election, which matches the procedural definition, though Mill adds safeguards for minorities.

premarital-sex.rationale: Private morality is outside the form-of-government doctrine; adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Government answerable to voters rests on free information and debate, as Mill argues, so shutdowns sit badly with it; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic programme is left to party competition, so the ideology is indifferent.

women-suffrage.rationale: Mill in Considerations on Representative Government holds difference of sex as irrelevant to political rights as height or hair colour, and modern representative democracies enfranchise women equally.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed by the theory of representation; adherents are split on the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Outside the scope of a form-of-government doctrine, with no common view among adherents.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Whether to set up such agencies is a policy matter for elected legislatures, so adherents are split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Representative democracy prescribes a form of rule, not a property theory, and the sources do not discuss first-come ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The sources do not address international courts, and adherents differ on external judicial authority over elected leaders.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the secular, constitutional basis of the model, in which law derives from elected legislators rather than scripture; not stated.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The model leaves such arrangements to those who write them; the sources do not address them.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The model says nothing about economic systems, which are left to party competition.

indirect-election.rationale: Adherents are split: Madison's Federalist No. 10 favours filtering opinion through chosen bodies, while Mill's Considerations rejected indirect election in favour of direct choice.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-constitutional mainstream of equal citizenship and religious liberty; not stated.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The sources do not address territorial autonomy, and adherents differ on it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the principle that governments rest on the consent of the governed, which supports letting residents vote on sovereignty; not stated.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources do not address decolonisation, and the model is neutral on it.

simple-living.rationale: The model is neutral on personal lifestyles.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The sources do not address Indigenous settlement, and the model is neutral on it.

equal-conscription.rationale: The model is neutral on conscription, which democracies have adopted and abandoned in varying forms.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The form of government says nothing about national spiritual ties; left to party competition.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Representative democracy rests on constitutional limits and due process, so killing without trial conflicts with its principles.

close-ties-china.rationale: A form of government is neutral on foreign alignment.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The form of government is neutral on this foreign-policy question.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: It prescribes how rulers are chosen, not who owns resources.

self-ownership.rationale: It is neutral on the philosophy of ownership; liberal and other traditions within it differ.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is left to elected majorities, not set by the system.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The form of government leaves welfare design to elected majorities.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: It works through elected representatives and parties; Madison defends the filtering role of intermediaries, so bypassing them contradicts it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Accountable elected government is generally opposed to special privilege, but the sources do not address it; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The form of government does not decide whether parties may organise by religion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The form of government is neutral on cultural values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Liberal-constitutional representative democracy usually carries equal rights before the law; the sources do not address divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: The form of government leaves resource control to elected governments.

missingStatements.text: Legislators should use their own judgment on behalf of voters rather than follow their instructions.
missingStatements.rationale: Burke's trustee model is the classic representative-democratic view, and Madison expects elected citizens to refine public opinion.

missingStatements.text: A legislature, not the executive, should hold the ultimate power to watch and control the government.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill says the proper office of a representative assembly is to watch and control the government.

missingStatements.text: Minorities should be given adequate representation in the legislature, not only the majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill states that adequate representation of minorities is an essential part of democracy.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universally endorsed in principle; proportional-representation covers the contested mechanism.

notes: Adherents split on electoral system, monarchy versus republic, and recall or referendums. Answers reflect Madison and Mill; the sources opened did not cover Mill's chapters on plural voting, the ballot and civil service in detail.
